source.title: Some open problems in spectral theory

accepted.question_text: Let H be a Hilbert space, let A be a closed densely defined self-adjoint operator on H, and let (L_k) be a sequence of finite-dimensional closed subspaces of Dom(A) whose orthogonal projections P_k converge strongly to the identity operator. If Spec(A,L_k) denotes the spectrum of the finite-dimensional compression P_k A: L_k -> L_k, does Spec(A,L_k) converge to Spec(A), in an appropriate limiting sense, as k -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Projection methods: Let (Lk )k∈N be a sequence of closed linear (finite dimensional) subspaces of Dom(A) such that the corresponding orthogonal projections Pk : H → Lk converge strongly to the identity operator I. Let Λ(A) be the set of all such sequences of subspaces.
Does lim k→∞ Spec(A,Lk ) = Spec(A) hold for self-adjoint operators?
Does lim k→∞ Spec(A,Lk ) = Spec(A) hold for self-adjoint operators? No!

accepted.question_text: Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space. For a finite-dimensional subspace L of Dom(A), define the second-order relative spectrum Spec2(A,L) as the set of complex numbers z for which there exists a nonzero u in L such that ((A - zI)u,(A - zI)v)=0 for every v in L. Given a sequence (L_k) of finite-dimensional approximation subspaces, is it true that the limiting second-order relative spectra lim_{k->infinity} Spec2(A,L_k) contain the whole spectrum Spec(A), rather than only the isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity known to be contained in the limit?

evidence.quote: M. Levitin & ES, 2004: Let L be a finite dimensional subspace of Dom(A). Then z ∈ C is said to belong to Spec2(A,L) if there exists u ∈ L \ {0} such that ((A − zI)u,(A − zI)v) = 0, ∀v ∈ L.
L. Boulton, 2006: lim k→∞ Spec2(A,Lk ) ⊇ {isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity}. Question: Is it true that lim k→∞ Spec2(A,Lk ) ⊇ Spec(A)?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a bounded linear operator on a Banach space X, and consider the resolvent norm function λ -> ||(A - λI)^(-1)|| on the resolvent set of A. Can a level set {λ in C : ||(A - λI)^(-1)|| = 1/ε} contain a nonempty open subset, equivalently can the resolvent norm take a finite constant value throughout an open set?
accepted.context_brief: Open level sets of the resolvent norm

evidence.quote: Let A : X → X be a bounded linear operator on a Banach space X. J. Globevnik 1976, A. Böttcher 1994: Can the level set {λ ∈ C : k(A − λI)−1 k = 1/ε} have an open subset? Can k(A − λI)−1 k take a finite constant value on an open set?
ES 2008: Yes ES and S. Shkarin 2009: Yes, even if X is separable, reflexive and strictly convex.

accepted.question_text: Let H be a Hilbert space and let A:H -> H be a closed densely defined operator that is the generator of a semigroup. Can the resolvent norm λ -> ||(A - λI)^(-1)|| be constant on a nonempty open subset of the resolvent set of A?

evidence.quote: Question (J. R. Partington): Let H be a Hilbert space and suppose a closed densely defined operator A : H → H is a generator of a semigroup. Can k(A − λI)−1 k be constant on an open set?
Hille-Yosida: k(A − λI)−1 k = O(1/λ) as λ → +∞.

accepted.question_text: Let T be the unit circle and define A on Fourier series by A(sum_{k=-infinity}^{infinity} c_k e^{ikt}) = sum_{k=-infinity}^{infinity} |k| c_k e^{ikt}; this is a first-order pseudodifferential operator on T with symbol |ξ|. Does there exist a function h:R_+ -> R_+ with h(τ) -> infinity as τ -> infinity such that, for every nonnegative smooth function q on T, the number of negative eigenvalues of A - qI is at least h(||q||_{L^1(T)})?
accepted.context_brief: Negative eigenvalues for periodic Hilbert-transform derivative perturbations

evidence.quote: Let A ( X∞ k=−∞ ckeikt) := X∞ k=−∞ |k|ckeikt ∼ first order ΨDO on the unit circle T with the symbol |ξ|; ∼ p −4 on T.
Question: Is there a function h : R+ → R+ such that h(τ ) → +∞ as τ → +∞ and Number of negative eigenvalues of A − qI ≥ h ( kqkL 1(T) ), ∀q ≥ 0, q ∈ C∞(T)?
